title: Rivers of India: a river's journey
instruction: Work through the chapter one step at a time.

hotspots.label: Gangotri Glacier
hotspots.text: The Bhagirathi starts here, from melting ice high in the Himalayas. Snow and glaciers keep Himalayan rivers flowing all year: they are perennial.

hotspots.label: Tehri Dam
hotspots.text: A large dam on the Bhagirathi. It stores water for drinking and irrigation and makes hydroelectric power.

hotspots.label: Devprayag
hotspots.text: Here the Bhagirathi and the Alaknanda meet. From this point on, the river is called the Ganga.

hotspots.label: Haridwar
hotspots.text: The Ganga leaves the mountains and enters the plains. It slows down and drops fertile silt along its banks.

hotspots.label: Prayagraj
hotspots.text: The Yamuna, the Ganga's longest tributary, joins it here. The meeting place is called a sangam.

hotspots.label: Sundarbans delta
hotspots.text: The Ganga and the Brahmaputra join and split into many channels before reaching the Bay of Bengal. Together they form the largest delta in the world, home to mangrove forests.

activity.doneText: You followed the river all the way to the sea!

activity.instruction: Move each river into the group it belongs to.
activity.intro: Rivers from the Himalayas are fed by snow and rain. Rivers of the peninsula depend mostly on rain.

items.say: The Ganga starts as the Bhagirathi at the Gangotri Glacier.
The Brahmaputra rises in Tibet, where it is called the Tsangpo.
The Indus rises in Tibet, near Lake Mansarovar.
The Yamuna rises at the Yamunotri Glacier.
The Godavari is the longest peninsular river.
The Krishna rises in the Western Ghats.
The Kaveri rises in the Brahmagiri hills of the Western Ghats.
The Narmada rises at Amarkantak and flows west.

activity.instruction: Sort the peninsular rivers by where they reach the sea.
activity.intro: East-flowing rivers drop their silt and build deltas. West-flowing rivers rush through narrow valleys and form estuaries.

items.say: The Godavari flows east into the Bay of Bengal.
The Mahanadi flows east into the Bay of Bengal.
The Krishna flows east into the Bay of Bengal.
The Kaveri flows east into the Bay of Bengal.
The Narmada flows west through a rift valley into the Arabian Sea.
The Tapi also flows west through a rift valley into the Arabian Sea.

activity.doneText: East makes deltas, west makes estuaries!

activity.instruction: Put the places on the Ganga's journey in order, from source to sea.
activity.intro: Put the stops in order, starting high in the mountains.

items.say: It begins as the Bhagirathi at the Gangotri Glacier.
At Devprayag the Alaknanda joins, and it becomes the Ganga.
At Haridwar it enters the plains.
At Prayagraj the Yamuna joins.
It flows on past Varanasi.
Finally it forms the Sundarbans delta and enters the Bay of Bengal.

activity.instruction: Tap the best answer. Read why after each question.
activity.intro: Time for a quick quiz on this chapter.

questions.q: At which place do the Bhagirathi and the Alaknanda join to form the Ganga?
questions.explain: The two rivers meet at Devprayag. From there, the river is called the Ganga.

questions.q: In Tibet, the Brahmaputra is known as the…
questions.explain: The Brahmaputra rises in Tibet, where it is called the Tsangpo, and enters India in Arunachal Pradesh.

questions.q: Which is the longest peninsular river?
questions.explain: The Godavari is the longest peninsular river. It is sometimes called the Dakshin Ganga.

questions.q: Himalayan rivers flow all year because they are fed by both rain and melting snow.
questions.explain: Glaciers and snow keep feeding them in the dry season too, so they are perennial.

questions.assertion: The Narmada does not form a delta.
questions.reason: It flows west through a narrow rift valley and enters the sea as an estuary.
questions.explain: Both are true. The fast flow through the rift valley carries silt away instead of building a delta.

questions.q: Which two rivers together form the Sundarbans delta?
questions.explain: The Ganga and the Brahmaputra build the world's largest delta before reaching the Bay of Bengal.
The Kaveri rises in the Brahmagiri hills of the Western Ghats and flows east.

questions.q: Which is the main reason peninsular rivers have little water in summer?
options: They flow into the Arabian Sea
questions.explain: Most peninsular rivers have no glaciers to feed them, so their flow drops in the dry months.
